note: Literature on SMAD2 and closely homologous SMAD3 supports genotype-phenotype distinctions between dominant-negative MH2 domain missense variants and haploinsufficient truncating variants.

evidence.text: SMAD2 pathogenic variants show phenotypic variability ranging from congenital heart defects with syndromic features to a late-onset vascular phenotype characterized by arterial aneurysms and connective tissue abnormalities.

source.title: Variable cardiovascular phenotypes associated with SMAD2 pathogenic variants
source.quote: Our data suggest two distinct phenotypes associated with pathogenic variants in SMAD2: complex CHD with or without laterality defects and other congenital anomalies, and a late-onset vascular phenotype characterized by arterial aneurysms with connective tissue abnormalities.

evidence.text: In homologous LDS3 (SMAD3), dominant-negative variants in the MH2 domain led to significantly earlier age of onset and more major vascular events compared to haploinsufficient variants.

source.title: Functional analysis of cell lines derived from SMAD3-related ...
source.quote: Individuals with dominant negative (DN) SMAD3 variant in the MH2 domain exhibited more major events (66.7% vs. 44.0%, P = 0.054), occurring at a younger age compared to those with haploinsufficient (HI) variants. The age at first major event was 35.0 years [IQR 29.0-47.0] in individuals with DN variants in MH2, compared to 46.0 years [IQR 40.0-54.0] in those with HI variants (P = 0.065).
